26-0171.description: Vice Chair Abdur-Rahman's resolution would give $975,000 to the Atlanta Volunteer Lawyers Foundation to support its services for survivors of intimate partner abuse and their families. The nonprofit runs the Safe Families Office in the Fulton County Courthouse, which the resolution says helps over 3,000 survivors a year and has lost federal funding. A revised version says the money would come, to the extent possible, from the county's opioid settlement funds rather than tax revenue.
26-0171.whyItMayMatter: Survivors of intimate partner abuse seeking legal help at the Fulton County Courthouse would have the Safe Families Office's services supported with county funds.

26-0191.description: Commissioner Ellis's resolution would authorize locality pay of up to $20,106 a year for Superior Court judges of the Atlanta Judicial Circuit who join the new state judicial pay plan, in place of the existing county salary supplement. The locality pay would automatically drop if the state raises judges' salaries. Judges would keep their county fringe and retirement benefits, the Chief Judge's supplement would continue, and judges who do not join the new plan would keep their current supplement.
26-0191.whyItMayMatter: Superior Court judges in the new state pay plan would receive county locality pay of up to $20,106 a year instead of the current county supplement.
